points.apply: Pray “Come, Lord Jesus” each night this week.

concl: Readiness is a habit, not a last-minute act.
Let us fill our flasks today.
2026-11-08.resolve: Never miss Sunday Mass this month.

intro: Theme: “Enter into the joy of your master.”
God is lavish with his gifts; fear buries them, trust multiplies them, and they are meant for the poor.

sub: A talent was twenty years' wages.
Each received according to ability.
No one is without gifts.
q: The LORD God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to till it and keep it.
To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, to each according to his ability. Then he went away.
points.apply: List three gifts God has given you.

sub: The third servant had a false image of God.
Fear paralyses love.
The reward is joy and more responsibility.
q: Happy is everyone who fears the LORD, who walks in his ways. You shall eat the fruit of the labor of your hands; you shall be happy, and it shall go well with you.
His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and trustworthy slave; you have been trustworthy in a few things, I will put you in charge of many things; enter into the joy of your master.’
points.apply: Dig up one buried talent this month.

points.h: Open your hand to the poor
sub: The capable woman works and gives.
Kindness to the poor is a loan to God.
World Day of the Poor.
q: She opens her hand to the poor, and reaches out her hands to the needy.
And the king will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.’
points.apply: Share a meal with a poor person this week.

concl: Every gift is a trust.
Use it with love, and share the Master's joy.
2026-11-15.resolve: Make a year-end account of your talents before Advent.

intro: Theme: “You did it to me.”
Christ the King reigns as Shepherd, is hidden in the least, and will reign until God is all in all.

sub: God himself seeks his scattered sheep.
He binds up and strengthens.
Jesus is the Good Shepherd who gives his life.
q: For thus says the Lord GOD: I myself will search for my sheep, and will seek them out. As shepherds seek out their flocks when they are among their scattered sheep, so I will seek out my sheep. I will rescue them from all the places to which they have been scattered on a day of clouds and thick darkness.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
points.apply: Seek out one person who has strayed from the parish.

points.h: The King hidden in the least
sub: The judgement is about love.
Christ identifies with the poor.
Both groups are surprised.
q: As for you, my flock, thus says the Lord GOD: I shall judge between sheep and sheep, between rams and goats.

Then the king will say to those at his right hand, ‘Come, you that are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world; for I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed me, I was naked and you gave me clothing, I was sick and you took care of me, I was in prison and you visited me.’
points.apply: Do one corporal work of mercy each day this week.

sub: Death is the last enemy.
Christ hands the Kingdom to the Father.
God will be all in all.
q: To him was given dominion and glory and kingship, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that shall not pass away, and his kingship is one that shall never be destroyed.

Then the seventh angel blew his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, saying, “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Messiah, and he will reign forever and ever.”
points.apply: Consecrate your family to Christ the King.

concl: Christ reigns through love.
Crown him today in the least of his brethren.
2026-11-22.resolve: Visit a prisoner, a hospital or an old-age home before Christmas.

intro: Theme: “Keep awake.”
Advent begins with longing, asks us to be reshaped by the Potter, and calls us to watch for Christ.

sub: A tired people cries to God.
They confess their sins honestly.
God answered in Jesus.
q: O that you would tear open the heavens and come down, so that the mountains would quake at your presence.
The one who testifies to these things says, “Surely I am coming soon.” Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!
points.apply: Pray “Come, Lord Jesus” at each Advent candle.

sub: God is our Father.
We are clay in the Potter's hands.
Advent is for reshaping.
q: Yet, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter.
Beware, keep alert; for you do not know when the time will come.
points.apply: Name one habit you want God to reshape.

sub: Four watches of the night.
The disciples slept in Gethsemane.
We watch with Christ in prayer.
q: For there is still a vision for the appointed time; it speaks of the end, and does not lie. If it seems to tarry, wait for it; it will surely come, it will not delay.

Therefore, keep awake—for you do not know when the master of the house will come, in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or at dawn, or else he may find you asleep when he comes suddenly. And what I say to you I say to all: Keep awake.
points.apply: Fix a daily time of prayer for Advent.

concl: Advent is longing, reshaping and watching.
The One who comes is faithful.
2026-11-29.resolve: Make your Advent Confession this week or next.

intro: Theme: “In the hand of God.”
All Souls: we pray for the faithful departed in the hope of the resurrection.

points.h: Our dead are in God's hands
sub: Death does not break the communion of saints.
Grief is real, but it is grief with hope.
God loses none of those given to his Son.
q: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will ever touch them.
And this is the will of him who sent me, that I should lose nothing of all that he has given me, but raise it up on the last day.
points.apply: Name your departed in prayer today.

sub: Purgatory is God's love completing his work.
Scripture shows prayer for the dead.
Above all we offer the Holy Mass for them.
q: But if he was looking to the splendid reward that is laid up for those who fall asleep in godliness, it was a holy and pious thought. Therefore he made atonement for the dead, so that they might be delivered from their sin.
Then he said to me, “These are they who have come out of the great ordeal; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.”
points.apply: Have a Mass offered for your departed.

sub: We believe in the resurrection of the body.
The grave is a resting place, not an end.
Live today so as to be ready.
q: For I know that my Redeemer lives, and that at the last he will stand upon the earth; and after my skin has been thus destroyed, then in my flesh I shall see God.
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live, and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
points.apply: Visit a cemetery this week and pray there.

concl: Love for our dead becomes prayer.
Their resurrection and ours is Christ's promise.
2026-11-02.resolve: Pray one decade of the rosary for the dead every day this month.

intro: Theme: “Come; for everything is ready now.”
The Lord who emptied himself invites all, especially the poor, to his banquet.

sub: Christ did not cling to his glory.
He became a servant to the point of the cross.
His humility is the pattern of our life.
q: See, my servant shall prosper; he shall be exalted and lifted up, and shall be very high.
For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.
points.apply: Choose the lowest place in one situation today.

sub: God's feast is prepared.
Good things become excuses when they come first.
The Eucharist is the banquet now.
q: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wines, of rich food filled with marrow, of well-aged wines strained clear.
At the time for the dinner he sent his slave to say to those who had been invited, ‘Come; for everything is ready now.’
points.apply: Name one excuse and drop it this week.

sub: The host's anger becomes generosity.
The poor and the lame fill the hall.
Our parish table must have room for them.
q: Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you that have no money, come, buy and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
Go out at once into the streets and lanes of the town and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.
points.apply: Invite someone who is usually left out.

concl: The humble Lord sets the table for the humble.
Come, and bring others with you.
2026-11-03.resolve: Attend one weekday Mass this week.

intro: Theme: “Count the cost.”
Jesus wants disciples who choose him with open eyes; God's grace makes the choice possible.

sub: No love may come before Christ.
The cross is the shape of love.
Following is daily, not occasional.
q: Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I shall show you.
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
points.apply: Accept one cross today without complaint.

sub: The tower and the king: think before you start.
Half-built faith is a sad sight.
Only God's help completes the building.
q: Unless the LORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain. Unless the LORD guards the city, the guard keeps watch in vain.
For which of you, intending to build a tower, does not first sit down and estimate the cost, to see whether he has enough to complete it?
points.apply: Renew one promise you made to God.

sub: God works in us the will and the deed.
A disciple shines in a crooked generation.
St Charles shone in the plague.
q: Those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the sky, and those who lead many to righteousness, like the stars forever and ever.
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
points.apply: Do one good work today for God's glory, not your own.

concl: Discipleship costs everything, and Christ is worth it.
God who calls also gives the strength.
2026-11-04.resolve: Read Luke 14:25–33 again tonight and examine your priorities.

intro: Theme: “Lost and found.”
God searches for the lost; heaven rejoices when they are found; and the found count everything as loss for Christ.

sub: Sinners came near to listen.
The grumblers stayed at a distance.
The shepherd goes after the one.
q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak, but the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will feed them with justice.
Which one of you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost until he finds it?
points.apply: Pray by name for one person who has strayed.

sub: God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked.
Conversion brings joy, not shame.
Confession is heaven's party.
q: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord GOD, and not rather that they should turn from their ways and live?
Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
points.apply: Plan a Confession this month.

sub: Paul's credentials were impressive.
Christ is worth more than all of them.
The found person sells everything for the treasure.
q: Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth that I desire other than you. My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which someone found and hid; then in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.
points.apply: Let go of one thing you are proud of and offer it to Christ.

concl: We are found by a searching God.
Let us rejoice with heaven and search with him.
2026-11-05.resolve: Reach out this week to someone who has drifted away.

intro: Theme: “Stewards with a heavenly passport.”
We will give an account; so let us be shrewd for eternity, as citizens of heaven.

sub: Everything we have is entrusted.
The manager's time ran out suddenly.
Ours will too.
q: For God will bring every deed into judgment, including every secret thing, whether good or evil.
So he summoned him and said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Give me an accounting of your management, because you cannot be my manager any longer.’
points.apply: Examine your conscience tonight as a steward.

sub: Jesus praises decisiveness, not dishonesty.
The world plans carefully for its goals.
The children of light must plan for theirs.
q: Go to the ant, you lazybones; consider its ways, and be wise.
And his master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly; for the children of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own generation than are the children of light.
points.apply: Set one concrete spiritual goal for this month.

sub: Some are enemies of the cross.
We await a Saviour from heaven.
Our home shapes our habits.
q: I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go to the house of the LORD!”
For here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the city that is to come.
points.apply: Spend time before the Blessed Sacrament this First Friday.

concl: We are stewards, not owners.
Live today as citizens of heaven.
2026-11-06.resolve: Write one spiritual goal for November and keep it where you see it.

intro: Theme: “One Master.”
Faithfulness in small things, freedom from money, contentment in Christ.

sub: Money is a small thing compared with the Kingdom.
Small honesty trains the heart.
God entrusts true riches to the faithful.
q: Remove far from me falsehood and lying; give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the food that I need.
Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.
points.apply: Be scrupulously honest in one small matter today.

sub: Wealth wants to rule.
Divided hearts serve neither well.
Generosity breaks money's hold.
q: Put no confidence in extortion, and set no vain hopes on robbery; if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.
No slave can serve two masters; for a slave will either hate the one and love the other, or be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
points.apply: Give a fixed share this week to the poor.

sub: The Pharisees justified themselves before others.
God sees beyond appearances.
Contentment comes from Christ, not from possessions.
q: For the LORD does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.
So he said to them, “You are those who justify yourselves in the sight of others; but God knows your hearts; for what is prized by human beings is an abomination in the sight of God.”
points.apply: Thank God tonight for three things you have.

concl: Serve God, and money becomes a servant.
In Christ we have enough.
2026-11-07.resolve: Decide on a regular share of your income for God and the poor.

intro: Theme: “The river from the Temple.”
The Lateran, mother of churches; Christ the true Temple; we the living temple of the Spirit.

sub: Ezekiel's river brings life everywhere.
Grace grows deeper as we go in.
The Church exists to give life.
q: Wherever the river goes, every living creature that swarms will live, and there will be very many fish, once these waters reach there. It will become fresh; and everything will live where the river goes.
Let anyone who is thirsty come to me, and let the one who believes in me drink. As the scripture has said, “Out of the believer's heart shall flow rivers of living water.”
points.apply: Bring one person closer to the sacraments this month.

sub: Jesus cleanses worship turned into business.
The true Temple is his Body.
He rebuilds it in three days.
q: It is zeal for your house that has consumed me; the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”… But he was speaking of the temple of his body.
points.apply: Keep silence and reverence in church.

sub: Heaven cannot contain God, yet he dwells with us.
We are the living stones.
Unity with the Pope keeps the building one.
q: But will God indeed dwell on the earth? Even heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built!
And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, “See, the home of God is among mortals. He will dwell with them; they will be his peoples, and God himself will be with them.”
points.apply: Pray for the Pope and your bishop today.

concl: Love the church building; become the living Church.
Let the river of grace flow through you.
2026-11-09.resolve: Arrive ten minutes early for Mass and pray in silence.

intro: Theme: “Grace, not wages.”
The grace of God has appeared; we serve freely, without keeping score.

points.h: The grace of God has appeared
sub: Christ's coming is pure gift.
Light has dawned on those in darkness.
Grace trains us, step by step.
q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who lived in a land of deep darkness—on them light has shined.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Thank God for one grace you did not earn.

sub: Paul gives counsel to old and young.
Holiness is practical.
Walk humbly with God.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
For who is greater, the one who is at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
points.apply: Choose one act of kindness and justice today.

sub: We cannot put God in our debt.
Service is love, not a bargain.
Freedom from keeping score.
q: What shall I return to the LORD for all his bounty to me?
So you also, when you have done all that you were ordered to do, say, ‘We are worthless slaves; we have done only what we ought to have done!’
points.apply: Serve someone today without telling anyone.

concl: All is grace.
We serve because we are loved.
2026-11-10.resolve: Read St Leo's Christmas sermon (Office of Readings, 25 Dec).

intro: Theme: “The one who returned.”
Cleansed by mercy, we turn back in thanks, and thanks becomes mercy.

sub: The lepers cried from a distance.
Healing came on the way.
Baptism is our cleansing.
q: So he went down and immersed himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God; his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.
When he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” And as they went, they were made clean.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises tonight.

sub: Nine took the gift and went.
One came back to the Giver.
Thanks turns healing into salvation.
q: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits.
Then one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, praising God with a loud voice. He prostrated himself at Jesus' feet and thanked him. And he was a Samaritan.
points.apply: Make your next prayer only thanksgiving.

sub: Martin shared his cloak.
He saw Christ in the beggar.
The grateful become generous.
q: Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover them, and not to hide yourself from your own kin?
And the king will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.’
points.apply: Give a garment to someone in need.

concl: Grace received calls for grace returned.
Be the one who comes back.
2026-11-11.resolve: Keep a gratitude list this week: three thanks each night.

intro: Theme: “The Kingdom among us.”
The Kingdom is present in Christ, transforms our relationships, and builds unity.

sub: Not in signs and dates.
Present in Jesus himself.
It comes through the Cross.
q: And in the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed, nor shall this kingdom be left to another people. It shall crush all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, and it shall stand forever.

Once Jesus was asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God was coming, and he answered, “The kingdom of God is not coming with things that can be observed; nor will they say, ‘Look, here it is!’ or ‘There it is!’ For, in fact, the kingdom of God is among you.”
points.apply: Look today for one quiet sign of God's Kingdom.

sub: Onesimus returns as a brother.
The Gospel changes how we see people.
Family is defined by doing God's will.
q: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Come closer to me.” And they came closer. He said, “I am your brother, Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt.”
For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.
points.apply: Treat someone who serves you as family.

sub: Josaphat worked for unity with Rome.
He died forgiving his killers.
Unity is Christ's prayer.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
That they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
points.apply: Pray for Christian unity today.

concl: The Kingdom grows among brothers and sisters.
Unity is its sign.
2026-11-12.resolve: Read the Letter to Philemon (one page) this week.

intro: Theme: “Do not look back.”
Be ready: not living as if God did not exist, not looking back, abiding in truth and love.

points.h: As in the days of Noah
sub: Ordinary life is not the sin.
Forgetting God is.
Noah obeyed while others carried on.
q: Noah did this; he did all that God commanded him.

Just as it was in the days of Noah, so too it will be in the days of the Son of Man. They were eating and drinking, and marrying and being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed all of them.
points.apply: Bring God into one ordinary task today.

sub: She was saved but looked back.
Longing for the old life is dangerous.
Losing life for Christ keeps it.
q: But Lot's wife, behind him, looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
Remember Lot's wife. Those who try to make their life secure will lose it, but those who lose their life will keep it.
points.apply: Renounce one thing you still look back at.

sub: Love is walking in his commandments.
Abide; do not go “beyond”.
Faithfulness keeps us ready.
q: Happy are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the law of the LORD.
This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.
points.apply: Read one paragraph of the Catechism daily.

concl: An undivided heart is ready for the Lord.
Look forward to him, not back.
2026-11-13.resolve: Make a daily examen this week before sleep.

intro: Theme: “Do not lose heart.”
Persistent prayer, trust in a just Father, and generosity to those who spread the Gospel.

sub: The widow kept coming.
Persistence is trust, not nagging.
Others can help hold up our arms.
q: Whenever Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; and whenever he lowered his hand, Amalek prevailed. But Moses' hands grew weary; so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side; so his hands were steady until the sun set.
Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray always and not to lose heart.
points.apply: Take up again a prayer you abandoned.

sub: The judge was unjust; God is not.
The cry of the poor reaches him.
The real question is our faith.
q: The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds, and it will not rest until it reaches its goal.

And will not God grant justice to his chosen ones who cry to him day and night? Will he delay long in helping them? I tell you, he will quickly grant justice to them. And yet, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth?
points.apply: Pray today for someone suffering injustice.

sub: Gaius welcomed strangers sent by the Church.
Hospitality supports mission.
We share in the work we support.
q: He said, “My lord, if I find favor with you, do not pass by your servant.”
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Give to the missions this week.

concl: Keep praying; God is listening.
Let him find faith in us.
2026-11-14.resolve: Choose one intention and pray for it daily until Advent.

intro: Theme: “Lord, let me see again.”
Cry out, return to first love, ask for sight and follow.

sub: The blind man heard Jesus passing.
The crowd tried to silence him.
He shouted all the more.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
Then he shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
points.apply: Pray the Jesus Prayer often today.

sub: Ephesus worked hard but grew cold.
Remember where you fell from.
Do the first works again.
q: Go and proclaim in the hearing of Jerusalem, Thus says the LORD: I remember the devotion of your youth, your love as a bride, how you followed me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.
But I have this against you, that you have abandoned the love you had at first. Remember then from what you have fallen; repent, and do the works you did at first.
points.apply: Take up one practice of your first fervour.

sub: Jesus asks what we want.
Faith names its need.
Healing leads to following.
q: Open my eyes, so that I may behold wondrous things out of your law.
“What do you want me to do for you?” He said, “Lord, let me see again.” Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight; your faith has saved you.”
points.apply: Ask Jesus plainly for what you need.

concl: Christ restores sight and love.
Follow him, glorifying God.
2026-11-16.resolve: Read Revelation 2–3 this week: the letters to the seven churches.

intro: Theme: “I stand at the door and knock.”
Christ knocks, warns against lukewarmness, and brings salvation to the house that opens.

sub: He does not force the door.
He waits for our response.
He wants to share a meal with us.
q: I slept, but my heart was awake. Listen! my beloved is knocking. “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one.”
Listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you, and you with me.
points.apply: Open one closed area of your life to Christ.

sub: Laodicea was rich and comfortable.
Comfort cooled its love.
God wants the whole heart.
q: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.
I know your works; you are neither cold nor hot. I wish that you were either cold or hot. So, because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I am about to spit you out of my mouth.
points.apply: Choose one fervent act of love for God today.

sub: Jesus calls Zacchaeus by name.
Grace first, then conversion.
Conversion opens the purse.
q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak.
Then Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham. For the Son of Man came to seek out and to save the lost.”
points.apply: Repair one injustice this week.

concl: Open the door; Christ is knocking.
Let your conversion reach your wallet.
2026-11-17.resolve: Give generously to the poor this week, as Elizabeth did.

intro: Theme: “Holy, holy, holy.”
Heaven's unceasing worship gives meaning to our faithful work while we wait for the King.

sub: The open door in heaven.
The song that never stops.
The Sanctus at every Mass.
q: And one called to another and said: “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.”
Day and night without ceasing they sing, “Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come.”
points.apply: Pray the Sanctus attentively at Mass.

sub: The King has gone and will return.
Each received the same pound.
Small trust leads to great responsibility.
q: The LORD God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to till it and keep it.
He said to him, ‘Well done, good slave! Because you have been trustworthy in a very small thing, take charge of ten cities.’
points.apply: Do one small duty with great care.

sub: Gifts grow when used.
The one who hid lost even what he had.
Work with all your strength now.
q: Whatever your hand finds to do, do with your might; for there is no work or thought or knowledge or wisdom in Sheol, to which you are going.
I tell you, to all those who have, more will be given; but from those who have nothing, even what they have will be taken away.
points.apply: Use one gift you have neglected.

concl: Our small work joins heaven's great song.
Be faithful until the King returns.
2026-11-18.resolve: Offer your work each morning to God this week.

intro: Theme: “The Lamb who weeps.”
The slain Lamb conquers, ransoms every nation, and weeps over those who do not recognise his visit.

sub: No one could open the scroll.
The Lion is a slaughtered Lamb.
Love conquers by giving itself.
q: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
Singing with full voice, “Worthy is the Lamb that was slaughtered to receive power and wealth and wisdom and might and honor and glory and blessing!”
points.apply: Pray the Agnus Dei slowly at Mass.

sub: God provided the Lamb.
His blood buys back all peoples.
The Church is catholic: from every tongue.
q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So the two of them walked on together.

They sing a new song: “You are worthy to take the scroll and to open its seals, for you were slaughtered and by your blood you ransomed for God saints from every tribe and language and people and nation.”
points.apply: Pray for the Church in a country other than your own.

sub: God grieves love refused.
Jerusalem missed its visitation.
He visits us today.
q: For these things I weep; my eyes flow with tears; for a comforter is far from me, one to revive my courage.
As he came near and saw the city, he wept over it, saying, “If you, even you, had only recognized on this day the things that make for peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.”
points.apply: Examine tonight where God visited you today.

concl: The Lamb conquers by love and weeps for us.
Recognise his visit and choose peace.
2026-11-19.resolve: Pray for peace in the world each day this week.

intro: Theme: “Sweet as honey.”
Eat God's word, delight in it, and keep God's house a house of prayer.

sub: Ezekiel and John ate the word.
It enters the prophet's life first.
Only then can he speak it.
q: He said to me, Mortal, eat this scroll that I give you and fill your stomach with it. Then I ate it; and in my mouth it was as sweet as honey.
So I took the little scroll from the hand of the angel and ate it; it was sweet as honey in my mouth, but when I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter.
points.apply: Read today's Gospel three times slowly.

sub: The word is delight.
The people hung on Jesus' words.
Love for Scripture grows with use.
q: How sweet are your words to my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
But they did not find anything they could do, for all the people were spellbound by what they heard.
points.apply: Memorise one verse this week.

sub: Jesus cleanses the Temple.
Worship must not become business.
Our hearts too need cleansing.
q: Has this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your sight? You know, I too am watching, says the LORD.
It is written, ‘My house shall be a house of prayer’; but you have made it a den of robbers.
points.apply: Set up a prayer corner at home.

concl: Eat the word, and it will make you a house of prayer.
Let Jesus teach daily in your temple.
2026-11-20.resolve: Read the Sunday Gospel at home every Saturday evening.

intro: Theme: “God of the living.”
To God all are alive; his breath raises his witnesses; Mary belonged wholly to him.

sub: The Sadducees mocked the resurrection.
God is still the God of the patriarchs.
To him all are alive.
q: He said further, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” And Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.

And the fact that the dead are raised Moses himself showed, in the story about the bush, where he speaks of the Lord as the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Now he is God not of the dead, but of the living; for to him all of them are alive.
points.apply: Pray for one departed person today.

sub: The witnesses were killed.
God's breath raised them.
The risen life is new, not a copy.
q: Thus says the Lord GOD to these bones: I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live.
Indeed they cannot die anymore, because they are like angels and are children of God, being children of the resurrection.
points.apply: Thank God for the gift of eternal life.

sub: Hannah gave Samuel to the Lord.
Mary belonged wholly to God from her youth.
She is the living temple.
q: For this child I prayed; and the LORD has granted me the petition that I made to him. Therefore I have lent him to the LORD; as long as he lives, he is given to the LORD.
Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” Then the angel departed from her.
points.apply: Renew your consecration to God through Mary.

concl: We belong to the God of the living.
With Mary, let us give ourselves wholly to him.
2026-11-21.resolve: Pray the Angelus daily this week.

intro: Theme: “All she had.”
Those who follow the Lamb give themselves wholly, as the widow did.

sub: The Lamb stands on Mount Zion.
His followers bear his name.
They go wherever he goes.
q: Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place? Those who have clean hands and pure hearts, who do not lift up their souls to what is false, and do not swear deceitfully.
Then I looked, and there was the Lamb, standing on Mount Zion! And with him were one hundred forty-four thousand who had his name and his Father's name written on their foreheads.
points.apply: Make the Sign of the Cross with attention today.

sub: The rich gave from surplus.
She gave her whole living.
God measures love and trust.
q: She went and did as Elijah said, so that she as well as he and her household ate for many days. The jar of meal was not emptied, neither did the jug of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke by Elijah.
He said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them; for all of them have contributed out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”
points.apply: Give something that costs you.

sub: Giving reveals the heart.
God looks on the heart.
Trust frees us to give.
q: For the LORD does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
points.apply: Review your giving this year honestly.

concl: Small gifts given wholly are great before God.
Follow the Lamb who gave everything.
2026-11-23.resolve: Decide on your Advent and Christmas giving to the poor now.

intro: Theme: “Do not be terrified.”
The Temple's stones fall, false prophets come, but the harvest belongs to God.

sub: The Temple was beautiful.
It would be destroyed in AD 70.
Only God's work lasts.
q: Unless the LORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain. Unless the LORD guards the city, the guard keeps watch in vain.
As for these things that you see, the days will come when not one stone will be left upon another; all will be thrown down.
points.apply: Build your life on prayer and the sacraments.

sub: Many will claim his name.
Date-setters are false prophets.
Wars do not mean the end is here.
q: Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, says the LORD.

And he said, “Beware that you are not led astray; for many will come in my name and say, ‘I am he!’ and, ‘The time is near!’ Do not go after them. When you hear of wars and insurrections, do not be terrified; for these things must take place first, but the end will not follow immediately.”
points.apply: Do not forward fearful end-times messages.

sub: The sickle belongs to God.
Wheat and weeds grow until harvest.
The martyrs were ripe wheat.
q: Put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Go in, tread, for the wine press is full. The vats overflow, for their wickedness is great.

Another angel came out of the temple, calling with a loud voice to the one who sat on the cloud, “Use your sickle and reap, for the hour to reap has come, because the harvest of the earth is fully ripe.”
points.apply: Pray for persecuted Christians.

concl: Our hope is calm because God holds history.
Let us ripen in faith like the martyrs.
2026-11-24.resolve: Learn the life of one Asian martyr this week.

intro: Theme: “By your endurance.”
Persecution becomes testimony; Christ gives wisdom; endurance ends in the song of the Lamb.

sub: Arrests, prisons, kings and governors.
Even family may betray.
Every trial is a chance to witness.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.

But before all this occurs, they will arrest you and persecute you; they will hand you over to synagogues and prisons, and you will be brought before kings and governors because of my name. This will give you an opportunity to testify.
points.apply: Witness calmly when your faith is questioned.

sub: Moses feared he could not speak.
God gives the words.
St Catherine answered the philosophers.
q: Now go, and I will be with your mouth and teach you what you are to speak.
For I will give you words and a wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to withstand or contradict.
points.apply: Learn one answer of the Catechism by heart.

sub: Israel sang after the sea.
The victors sing after the trial.
Endurance ends in praise.
q: The LORD is my strength and my might, and he has become my salvation; this is my God, and I will praise him, my father's God, and I will exalt him.
And they sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb: “Great and amazing are your deeds, Lord God the Almighty! Just and true are your ways, King of the nations!”
points.apply: Praise God today in the middle of a difficulty.

concl: Not a hair of your head will perish.
Endure, and you will sing.
2026-11-25.resolve: Keep one good resolution steadily until Christmas.

intro: Theme: “Raise your heads.”
When the world shakes, disciples look up: Babylon falls, and the Lamb's wedding feast is near.

sub: Signs in the heavens, distress on earth.
Others faint with fear.
Disciples look up to their Redeemer.
q: It will be said on that day, Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, so that he might save us. This is the LORD for whom we have waited; let us be glad and rejoice in his salvation.
Then they will see ‘the Son of Man coming in a cloud’ with power and great glory. Now when these things begin to take place, stand up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.
points.apply: Pray a prayer of trust when you hear bad news.

sub: Babylon is the city of pride and luxury.
Empires built on pride end in ruins.
Do not build your life on it.
q: Then he responded, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the images of her gods lie shattered on the ground.”
He called out with a mighty voice, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great!”
points.apply: Renounce one luxury this Advent and give its cost to the poor.

points.h: The marriage supper of the Lamb
sub: God prepares a feast for all peoples.
The Bride is invited.
Every Mass is a foretaste.
q: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wines, of rich food filled with marrow, of well-aged wines strained clear.
And the angel said to me, “Write this: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.” And he said to me, “These are true words of God.”
points.apply: Prepare carefully for Communion this Sunday.

concl: Look up: your redemption is near.
The feast is ready; come.
2026-11-26.resolve: Make a good Confession before Advent begins.

intro: Theme: “All things new.”
Christ's words outlast the universe; the book of life is opened; God makes a new heaven and a new earth.

sub: The fig tree tells the season.
Heaven and earth will pass.
Christ's word remains.
q: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
points.apply: Carry a Gospel verse with you this week.

sub: The dead stand before the throne.
Works are judged.
Names are written by grace.
q: But at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who is found written in the book.

And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne, and books were opened. Also another book was opened, the book of life. And the dead were judged according to their works, as recorded in the books.
points.apply: Examine your conscience on this year's works.

sub: God creates new heavens and earth.
The new Jerusalem comes down as a bride.
Creation is transformed, not discarded.
q: For I am about to create new heavens and a new earth; the former things shall not be remembered or come to mind.

Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth; for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more. And I saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
points.apply: Care for creation in one concrete way.

concl: Build on the word that does not pass.
God is making all things new.

intro: Theme: “Come, Lord Jesus.”
The year ends with the river of life and the tree of healing; be alert in prayer; Advent begins.

sub: The river flows from the throne.
The tree of life returns.
Its leaves heal the nations.
q: On the banks, on both sides of the river, there will grow all kinds of trees for food. Their leaves will not wither nor their fruit fail, but they will bear fresh fruit every month, because the water for them flows from the sanctuary. Their fruit will be for food, and their leaves for healing.

Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb through the middle of the street of the city. On either side of the river is the tree of life with its twelve kinds of fruit, producing its fruit each month; and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.
points.apply: Thank God for one healing grace this year.

sub: Guard against heaviness of heart.
Worries can crowd out God.
Prayer gives strength to stand.
q: O come, let us worship and bow down, let us kneel before the LORD, our Maker! For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. O that today you would listen to his voice!

Be on guard so that your hearts are not weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness and the worries of this life, and that day does not catch you unexpectedly, like a trap. For it will come upon all who live on the face of the whole earth. Be alert at all times, praying that you may have the strength to escape all these things that will take place, and to stand before the Son of Man.
points.apply: Choose one Advent fast.

sub: God himself will be the light.
The promise: I am coming soon.
Advent begins tonight.
q: The sun shall no longer be your light by day, nor for brightness shall the moon give light to you by night; but the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.
And there will be no more night; they need no light of lamp or sun, for the Lord God will be their light, and they will reign forever and ever.
points.apply: Light the first Advent candle tomorrow with your family.

concl: The year closes in light.
Marana tha: Come, Lord Jesus!
2026-11-28.resolve: Plan your family's Advent prayer tonight.

intro: Theme: “We have found the Messiah.”
Andrew, the First-Called, follows at once and brings others to Jesus.

sub: Andrew followed after the Baptist's word.
He left his nets immediately.
Advent asks what nets hold us.
q: I am now sending for many fishermen, says the LORD, and they shall catch them.

As he walked by the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea—for they were fishermen. And he said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
points.apply: Leave one distraction this Advent.

sub: Andrew ran to his brother.
Mission begins at home.
Without Andrew, no Peter?
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”

He first found his brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated Anointed). He brought Simon to Jesus, who looked at him and said, “You are Simon son of John. You are to be called Cephas” (which is translated Peter).
points.apply: Invite one family member to Mass.

sub: Faith comes from hearing.
Someone must speak.
The voice goes to the ends of the earth.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.”
points.apply: Share your faith with one person this week.

concl: Someone brought us to Jesus.
Now we bring others.
2026-11-30.resolve: Pray the St Andrew Christmas novena daily until Christmas.
